register_note: A measured deep dive in Quant's own identity (white page, warm near-black, one orange), half of it hand-drawn whiteboard, one continuous drone bed, gear 2 throughout with gear 1 screen-share reads and one gear 3 landing line. The motion language is QUIET: the paper sheet, the house cross-fade + scale-in, a warm film burn on every screen-share edge, one 3D card move, and exactly one spin and one melt, both inside the C1 system-diagram run, the only diagram marquee in the video. Screen-share face mode (house rule #1b): no punch-ins, no light leaks, no glitch on any face join.

card_pick.why: The gated card slot blocks flip (left-behind) and slide sits inside the last three videos (reset 2026-10-30). cube was last used 2026-10-27 (five videos back), it is a Safe CSS-3D pick with no render-flag risk, and its one clean 3D turn is the only 3D language in the video: the spin-3d marquee in CH2 echoes it. One linear-timed cube turn, around 0.6 s, on every title card. book-flip and swap are fresh and the page-turn would suit a paper video, but both need the canvas-draw-element render flag, which is unverified in our render chain: see open_questions.

face_glitch_pick.why: Every FACE window is Mike's OBS screen share: a white deck area, his webcam bottom-right, the CTA box top-right. A warm radial flash reads as light on paper and keeps the Quant identity intact; a Blocks Max block-shatter is a tech-hype hard cut and would fight the calm register on 17 edges. Advisory slot: the previous video also used film-burn, Blocks was last used 2026-10-27; fit comes first here. Intensity dialed low so the eight cut-in / cut-out pairs never strobe.

face_leak_set.why: FACE MODE = SCREEN SHARE (house rule #1b): a screen share is never zoomed, so this video has no punch-ins and no light leaks. The gated face_leak slot carries nothing. Had leaks been needed the fresh set would have been lightleaks-soft-2 / -3 / -4 (the previous video's lightleaks-soft-1 is BLOCKED).

melt_pick.why: Nothing is blocked (left-behind used no melt); both looks sit inside the last three videos, MELT/RGB (reset 2026-10-30) is the less recent. Fit: the RGB melt is a pure affine channel split that runs on live video and on stills, so it is safe on the C1 diagram still; the SOFT falloff variant (melt-rgb-soft-1, medium energy, 0.84 s) is the quietest melt in the catalog, right for a gear 2 explainer. The Equidistant spherical vortex is image-only in its engine and reads surreal, wrong for a white-page diagram. ONE use.

spin_pick.why: Nothing is blocked (left-behind used no spin); SPIN/Center Ease (lets-get-rich) and SPIN/3D Side Ease (reset) sit in the last three videos. SPIN/3D Center Ease is the LEAST recently used spin look on the ledger (golden-kitty, 2026-10-02) and it is a real 3D turn, so it echoes the cube card and keeps one 3D vocabulary. The short variant (0.44 s) keeps the turn under the register. Mirrored padding, full-frame, the spine never shows. ONE use.

consistency_check: ONE card move (rmn:cube on all five title cards T2 to T6) · ONE face pick (hand:film-burn on all 17 face edges, 8 cut-ins + 9 cut-outs; F1 opens on the face so it has no cut-in) · ONE melt look (MELT/RGB, melt-rgb-soft-1, one use) · ONE spin look (SPIN/3D Center Ease, spin-3d-center-ease-short-t-cw, one use) · text containers, deck cards and receipts stay on the house cross-fade + 0.93 to 1 scale-in (10 rows) · the whiteboard paper sheet on its 8 own cuts · the two receipts-as-objects ride two different motion-3d-pan variants (no SFX) · CLIP-1 insert-in + insert-out hand:fade 0.5 s · no glitch rows (no AI stills, no Envato video in this video) · no punch / leak rows (screen-share face mode) · melt and spin both sfx_duck true · no em dashes.
open_questions: Card move: rmn:cube is the Safe pick. book-flip is fresh on the ledger and a page-turn fits a paper whiteboard video better than any other card move, but it (and swap) draws HTML into canvas and needs Chrome's canvas-draw-element flag in the headless renderer, which we have never wired. If Mike accepts that risk and the comp-builder verifies the flag on a test render, swap card_pick to rmn:book-flip; otherwise cube ships.

Marquee moves on a calm white video: one short 3D spin (197.6) and one soft RGB melt (203.8) sit inside the C1 diagram run. They are the only library transitions with sound in the whole video and they are ducked under the VO. If Mike wants the paper register fully quiet, drop both (melt_spin_budget 0 / 0) and the two cuts fall back to the house cross-fade + scale-in.

F3 cut-in at 207.267 vs the T3 pause at 207.315: the CUE-SHEET holds C1-right-labels into the pause and lets T3's exit reveal the screen share, so the film burn at 207.27 is effectively absorbed by the card. The row stands (every face edge carries the pick); the comp-builder decides whether the burn peaks with the card's exit or is suppressed there.

Face pick: hand:film-burn repeats the previous video (advisory slot, not gated). The register decides it here; the alternative is lib:blocks-max-1/2/3 on every screen-share edge, which Mike can rule if he wants the harder cut.

R-ROSALIND (309.9, 4.8 s slot) and R-DENTSU (329.7, 3.8 s slot) ride 5 s motion-3d-pan engines, so the comp clips each move to its slot; R-DENTSU's slot ends in the T4 card pause. COVER-PLAN says push for R-DENTSU, the EDIT-PLAN and this plan say pan; confirm pan or revert to the push.
